title: ToolApiV1dot8
description: K-09 Tool API v1.8, a minor version for an unmapped turn's end at the gate (T-1219; T-1157's card a0; DL-457; README 'v1.8'): gateAndCommit takes K-02 v1.2's contextAndDecide (../model/model.v1.2.schema.json, frozen by T-1157), so decide's result may hold a read the AI layer's validator refused, in its place and with no output (K-02 v1.2 refusedRead), and the unmapped turn's end (decideResult.end oneQuestion: CQ-162 (a), 'a turn still unmapped ends in one question with nothing changed'), and its answer holds that end: asked once for the turn (gateAndCommit.committed end), every part decide kept asked with no limit run, and no row written for any part. It only adds to v1.6 (tool-api.v1.6.schema.json, frozen by T-1173 and unchanged, referred to here, which refers to v1.5 to v1): every v1.6 definition is here under its own name, the unchanged ones by reference; the changed ones (gateAndCommit.request, whose decided input is K-02 v1.2's pair, every K-02 v1 and v1.1 pair being one; gateAndCommit.committed and gateAndCommit.response, which may hold end; gateAndCommit.exchange, which ties the answer's end to the request's) take every earlier value, so every v1 to v1.6 exchange is a v1.8 exchange. v1.7 is T-054's journey 7 freeze, not merged when this one was frozen, so v1.8 refers to v1.6, not v1.7 (README 'v1.8', open gap 130). Added: no call, no key and no error; the answer's end; the named rule unmappedEndAsked (tool-api.rules.mjs). Each call's read, repeat and time budget are v1's (README 'Reads, repeats and time budgets'). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

gateAndCommit.request.title: GateAndCommitRequest
gateAndCommit.request.description: Gate and commit a turn, as v1.5 (arch 02 line 121; arch 06 lines 295 to 309; arch 10 line 508; K-05 v1 commitTurn and fireClock; README 'Reads, repeats and time budgets': the primary, uncached; the turn id is the key; at most 300 ms), with one change (v1.8, T-1219; README 'v1.8'): decided texts carry K-02 v1.2's contextAndDecide, so decide's result may hold a read the AI layer's validator refused, in its place and with no output (K-02 v1.2 refusedRead), and the unmapped turn's end (decideResult.end oneQuestion; CQ-162 (a)), on which the gate runs no limit, the commit writes no row for any part and the call answers asked once for the turn (gateAndCommit.committed end; README v1.8 defaults 142 to 145). Everything else is v1.5's, restated here with the same keywords (the planner's and the core actions' descriptions also name the end): the caller, the turn, a clock's firing, a core-only input, the planner's verb, the core actions, 'now', and the turn's rule (if, then, else: only a clock's firing may come with no turn, and a clock's turn carries no service and no chat id). Every K-02 v1 and v1.1 pair is a K-02 v1.2 pair, so every v1 to v1.6 request is a v1.8 request.

turn.description: The turn row the commit writes (K-05 v1 turn); every input but a clock's needs one. For a clock's firing (input.kind clock), the clock turn on the clock row's handle, or null when the firing's writes hold no outbox row (K-05 v1 fireClock.request.turn), as for any row no handle owns (K-04 turns.handle_id is not null). A clock turn has no texts: its one event id is the clock row's id (K-05 v1 default 9), its id is that event id's hash, as every turn's is (CQ-09), so one row's firing has one turn id and a repeat finds the first firing, and its trace id is the firing's own (CQ-06); its caller.kind is turn, with caller.turnId and caller.requestId its id. A firing with no turn is called with caller.kind clockFiring, caller.turnId null and caller.requestId the clock row's id. The named rule clockTurn checks these. From v1.5 the turn is gateAndCommit.turn: K-05 v1's turn, with the service and the chat id the runtime caller copies from the K-06 event of the turn's last text (README v1.5 default 135), which the commit leaves out of the turn row it writes.

input.description: What the turn acts on, as v1.5: decided texts (from v1.8 K-02 v1.2's pair), a clock's firing, or only core actions (the guard's keyword-only texts: arch 02 line 115).

oneOf.title: DecidedInput
oneOf.description: Decided texts: the context and decide's result, from v1.8 K-02 v1.2's pair, and the planner's verb, as v1.5. On the unmapped end nothing changes for any part, so the planner has no verb (planner null; README v1.8 default 144).

decided.description: The context and decide's result, as the gate reads them (K-02 v1.2 contextAndDecide: v1.1's pair, whose decide result may also hold refused reads and the unmapped turn's end; K-02 README 'v1.2'). Its named rules are the gate's: optionOffered and quoteInText, which read a K-02 read's output and the result's kept parts, so both skip a refused read, which holds no output.

planner.description: The planner's verb when nothing fit after meaning search; null otherwise, and on the unmapped end.

if.description: decide's result holds the unmapped turn's end (K-02 v1.2 decideResult.end).

then.description: The planner commits no verb on the unmapped end (README v1.8 default 144).

oneOf.title: ClockInput
oneOf.description: A clock's firing runs its step's clock branch, the safe default and who is told, with no decide reads (QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-4; arch 02 line 127), and answers fired (gateAndCommit.response), or notArmed, notDue or the clock row's versionChanged (gateAndCommit.errors). A version change on a row the branch read reloads once and runs the branch again, as limit 4 does (arch 06 line 305).

clockRowId.description: The clock row firing (K-05 v1 fireClock).

by.description: As K-05 v1 fireClock.request.by: the actor's alarm, the minute sweep, or staging's Fire now (BP 9.4).

jobId.description: The firing's job id for the event log (K-05 v1 fireClock).

oneOf.title: CoreOnlyInput
oneOf.description: Only core actions: STOP, START, HELP and the like, which code alone acts on (arch 02 line 115).

core.description: Shared-core calls this turn commits, in order (README 'In a turn or alone'). Each of the turn's texts carries one recordSafetyOutcome, whatever its outcome, since K-34 v1 writes one outcome row per text under the turn that joins it (README default 5); a clock's turn carries none. On the unmapped end they commit as in any turn (README v1.8 default 143).

now.description: The time the gate reads 'now' at.

then.description: A clock's firing: its turn may be null (K-05 v1 fireClock.request.turn); the named rule clockTurn checks the caller and the turn's id rule. A clock's turn has no text, so it carries no service and no chat id (v1.5; README v1.5 default 135).

else.description: Decided texts or core actions only: the turn is required (K-05 v1 commitTurn), as gateAndCommit.turn: the runtime caller fills its service and chat id from the turn's last text (v1.5; README v1.5 default 135).

gateAndCommit.response.title: GateAndCommitResponse
gateAndCommit.response.description: committed for a turn's decided texts or core actions (gateAndCommit.committed; v1.8: it may hold the unmapped turn's end, asked); fired for a clock's firing (as v1; K-05 v1 fireClock.response).

gateAndCommit.committed.title: GateAndCommitCommitted
gateAndCommit.committed.description: Committed, as v1.4's (which v1.5 and v1.6 refer to), its fields word for word, with one field more (v1.8, T-1219; README 'v1.8'): end, the turn's unmapped end answered asked once for the turn. An answer that holds end gated no part and wrote no row for one (dependentSchemas; README v1.8 defaults 142 and 143); the turn's core actions commit as in any turn. No v1 to v1.6 answer holds end, so every one is a v1.8 committed answer.

repeated.description: true when this turn id had committed before: nothing was written and the first commit comes back (K-05 v1 commitTurn).

parts.description: One result per decide part, in order; empty for a core-only turn.

planner.description: The planner's verb as committed; null when no planner ran, or when code refused its output.

core.description: One result per core action, in the request's order (v1.1's coreResult).

written.description: What the commit wrote (K-05 v1 commitResult).

effects.description: Effect rows written in the commit, to run after it (K-07 v1; K-05 v1.1).

end.title: TurnEnd
end.description: v1.8: the turn's unmapped end, answered (README v1.8 defaults 142 to 145). Set when the request's decided result holds K-02 v1.2's end (decideResult.end oneQuestion: a read of the turn was refused, and still refused after the one re-read; CQ-162 (a): 'a turn still unmapped ends in one question with nothing changed'), and only then (gateAndCommit.exchange): asked, the turn's one question, once for the turn and never one per part (K-02 v1.2 default 12); the gate ran no limit and the commit wrote no row for any part. Absent on every other answer, as in v1 to v1.6.

An answer that holds end gated and wrote nothing for any part (README v1.8 defaults 142 to 144): each part decide kept is asked, as v1 answers a part decide ended in one question, with no limit run (each limit notChecked, with no outcome), no stop, no key and nothing it depends on; the planner committed no verb; and written.written is empty, since neither a part nor a walk wrote a row (a core action's rows are named in its response, never there: default 134). The turn's core actions commit as in any turn: their lines stay in written.outboxRows, and promoted, effects and openQuestions hold what they wrote (default 143).

parts.description: Every part decide kept (K-02 v1.2 default 14), asked: no limit ran for it (arch 06 line 289: 'Still unclear: one question; nothing changes for that part').

planner.description: No planner verb on the unmapped end (README v1.8 default 144).

written.description: No versioned row of a part or a walk (README v1.8 default 143; K-05 v1 commitResult).

gateAndCommit.exchange.title: GateAndCommitExchange
gateAndCommit.exchange.description: One gateAndCommit request with its outcome, as v1.5, its request and its committed answer v1.8's: a request whose decided result holds K-02 v1.2's unmapped end is answered, when it commits, with end asked, once for the turn; every other request's answer holds no end (README 'v1.8', default 145). An error answers either, as v1.5's errors do.

if.description: The request's decided result holds K-02 v1.2's unmapped end (decideResult.end).

then.description: The unmapped end is answered asked once for the turn: a committed answer holds end (README v1.8 default 145).

else.description: Any other request: its answer holds no end, as in v1 to v1.6.
